input.strategy_title: GPU chargeback reporting for platform administrators
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Platform teams fund shared GPU clusters but cannot attribute consumption to the
projects using them, so capacity costs are socialized and heavy users have no
incentive to release resources. The in-flight metering strategy
(RHAISTRAT-9990) is delivering per-project GPU-hour usage data; this strategy
builds the administrator-facing chargeback reporting on top of that data. The
metering data schema is owned by RHAISTRAT-9990 and is not final until that
strategy lands — reporting work here consumes it, and must not re-implement
collection.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Administrators can view per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over selectable time ranges, computed from the metering data delivered by RHAISTRAT-9990. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Reports can be exported as CSV and retrieved via a stable API for finance tooling. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | The Dashboard admin view shows current-month consumption against each project's Kueue quota. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers report semantics (what counts as a GPU-hour) and export integration. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Distributed Workloads

## Out of Scope

- The metering collection pipeline itself (RHAISTRAT-9990)
- Currency/cost-rate modelling — reports are in GPU-hours, not dollars

## Open Questions

1. The metering data schema finalizes only when RHAISTRAT-9990 lands; report
   implementation consuming it carries that external timing risk.

# Per-project GPU-hour report computation and export API

## Description

This epic delivers the backend reporting capability for GPU chargeback: computation of per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over selectable time ranges, built on top of the per-project GPU-hour usage data delivered by the in-flight GPU usage metering strategy (RHAISTRAT-9990), plus CSV export and a stable API that finance tooling can retrieve reports through. It does not re-implement or alter the metering collection pipeline — it consumes its output.

## Scope

- Compute per-project GPU-hour consumption totals and time-bucketed reports over administrator-selectable time ranges, sourcing all usage data from the metering data delivered by the GPU usage metering strategy.
- Expose the computed reports through a stable API suitable for finance tooling retrieval.
- Provide CSV export of report results.
- Define and document the report output contract (fields, time-range semantics) that the administrator-facing Dashboard views and finance integrations build against.
- Isolate the consumption of the metering data schema (owned by the metering strategy, not yet final) in the input mapping, so report semantics are decoupled from the upstream schema.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given per-project GPU-hour metering data as delivered by the GPU usage metering work, when a report is requested for a selectable time range, then per-project GPU-hour consumption totals are returned that reconcile with the underlying metered usage for that range.
- Report results are exportable as CSV and retrievable via the stable API by a finance-tooling client, with the API contract documented.
- A change to the metering data schema delivered by the metering strategy is absorbed in the input mapping without redesigning the report computation or the report output contract (rework is limited to the metering-data input mapping).
- Report computation is validated end-to-end against metered usage data for at least one selectable time range, demonstrating correct attribution of consumption to projects.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over selectable time ranges, computed from the metering data — this epic delivers the computation half.
- HLR-2 (P1, bundled): CSV export and stable API retrieval for finance tooling — bundled with the P0 computation because both are output modes of the same aggregation over the same metering data on the same service surface; splitting would duplicate the aggregation and add an artificial boundary between one API surface.

## Risks / Notes

- The metering data schema finalizes only when the GPU usage metering strategy (RHAISTRAT-9990) lands; that external timing is outside this epic's control and may force rework in the input mapping. The schema-isolation acceptance criterion above confines that rework surface.

# Administrator chargeback reporting views in the Dashboard

## Description

This epic delivers the administrator-facing reporting experience in the Dashboard: per-project GPU-hour consumption reports viewable over selectable time ranges, and an admin view showing current-month consumption against each project's Kueue quota. It consumes the report computation and export capability delivered by the report computation and export API work; it adds no data collection or aggregation of its own.

## Scope

- Add an administrator-facing view of per-project GPU-hour consumption reports with selectable time ranges, reading computed report data from the report API.
- Add an admin view showing current-month per-project consumption against each project's Kueue quota, sourcing quota information from the Kueue quota objects the Dashboard already reads through the Kubernetes API.
- Present both capabilities within the existing Dashboard administrator surfaces, consistent with current Dashboard navigation and role handling for administrator-facing sections.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given computed per-project GPU-hour report data, when an administrator selects a time range, then the Dashboard shows per-project GPU-hour consumption for that range.
- Given current-month consumption data and each project's Kueue quota, when an administrator opens the admin consumption view, then current-month consumption is displayed against each project's Kueue quota.
- The reporting views are accessible to platform administrators through the existing Dashboard console without new private component APIs or data-plane ownership in the Dashboard.
- Report data displayed in the views reconciles with the same report retrieved via the export API for the identical time range.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): administrators can view per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over selectable time ranges — this epic delivers the administrator-facing view half.
- HLR-3 (P1, bundled): Dashboard admin view showing current-month consumption against each project's Kueue quota — bundled with the P0 report view because it is another presentation in the same administrator view surface consuming the same report data; splitting would build the same admin view surface twice.

## Risks / Notes

- Quota semantics follow the platform's Kueue quota model (ClusterQueue/LocalQueue); no quota-side backend work is expected — the Dashboard reads quota through the Kubernetes API today.
- The metering data schema risk carried by the report computation work propagates here only through the report API contract, which is defined within this strategy.

# Chargeback reporting documentation

## Description

This epic delivers the documentation for GPU chargeback reporting: report semantics (including what counts as a GPU-hour) and export integration for finance tooling. It is authored after the reporting implementation is complete so the content describes what was actually built.

## Scope

- Document report semantics: what a GPU-hour is as counted by the metering data, how per-project attribution works, and how selectable time ranges are interpreted.
- Document export integration: how finance tooling retrieves reports via the stable API and CSV export, including the report output contract.
- Document the administrator reporting views: where to find them and how to read the current-month consumption-vs-Kueue-quota display.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation covers report semantics, including a precise definition of what counts as a GPU-hour and how consumption is attributed to projects.
- Published documentation covers export integration for finance tooling, covering both CSV export and stable API retrieval against the documented report contract.
- The content is technically reviewed against the implemented reporting capability (computation, export, and Dashboard views) and reflects the behavior as built, including any metering-schema-driven caveats.
- Documentation includes worked examples of retrieving a report for a selectable time range via the export paths.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation covers report semantics (what counts as a GPU-hour) and export integration — fully covered by this epic.

## Risks / Notes

- The "what counts as a GPU-hour" definition originates in the GPU usage metering strategy's semantics; this epic documents it as landed, and is therefore sequenced after the reporting implementation.
- Owning team is not specified in the strategy; assigned to the team owning the report computation and export API (the primary documented surface) — confirm at planning.
